events.title: Constitution signed
events.summary: Muzaffar ad Din Shah signed the constitution on 30 December 1906, providing for an elected Majlis; he died five days later. Supplementary Fundamental Laws followed in 1907.

events.title: Anglo-Russian Agreement
events.summary: Britain and Russia agreed to divide Iran into spheres of influence (Russian north, British south and east, neutral centre).

events.title: Majlis bombarded
events.summary: Mohammad Ali Shah used the Russian-officered Persian Cossacks Brigade to bomb the Majlis building and close the assembly.

events.title: Constitution restored
events.summary: Constitutional forces marched on Tehran from Rasht and Esfahan, deposed Mohammad Ali Shah and re-established the constitution.

events.title: Majlis closed after Russian ultimatum
events.summary: After the Majlis refused a Russian ultimatum demanding the dismissal of treasurer-general Morgan Shuster, Bakhtiari chiefs surrounded the Majlis and forced acceptance; the constitution was again suspended.

events.title: Anglo-Persian Agreement
events.summary: Lord Curzon's proposed agreement (loan and British advisers) was widely viewed as a British protectorate; the Majlis refused to approve it.

events.title: Reza Khan and Sayyid Zia march into Tehran
events.summary: Cossack officer Reza Khan, with journalist Sayyid Zia ad Din Tabatabai, seized power.

events.title: Qajar dynasty deposed
events.summary: A Majlis dominated by Reza Khan's supporters deposed the Qajars; in December it conferred the crown on Reza Khan and his heirs.

events.title: Reza Shah crowned
events.summary: Reza Khan was crowned Reza Shah Pahlavi in April 1926.
events.note: A Commons file gives 25 April 1926 for the ceremony; that specific day is NOT yet confirmed by a tier A/B source.

events.title: Civil code enacted
events.summary: The civil code drafted under Justice Minister Ali Akbar Davar was enacted between 1927 and 1932 as part of a secular codification of law.

events.title: Capitulations abolished
events.summary: Reza Shah abolished the capitulations under which Europeans were subject to their own consular courts.

events.title: University of Tehran
events.summary: LoC records the country's first European-style university as established in 1935. Other sources give 1934 for its inauguration.
events.note: 1934 vs 1935. Say 'established in the mid-1930s' unless a primary source (e.g. the founding law) is cited.

events.title: Imam Reza shrine confrontation, Mashhad
events.summary: Troops entered the Imam Reza shrine where worshippers had gathered to protest the reforms; dozens were killed and many injured.

events.title: Ban on the veil
events.summary: A decree of 8 January 1936 banned veils (headscarf and chador) and was enforced forcefully; LoC records that the veil was 'forcibly abolished' in 1936.
events.note: Day-level date from Wikipedia only; year from LoC.

events.title: Trans-Iranian Railway fully opened
events.summary: The 1,394 km line linking the Caspian Sea with the Persian Gulf opened fully in 1938 (UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2021).

events.title: Anglo-Soviet invasion
events.summary: Britain and the Soviet Union invaded Iran. Most sources give 25 August 1941; LoC gives 26 August.
events.note: Date discrepancy: say 'late August 1941' or '25 August' with the LoC variance noted.

events.title: Reza Shah abdicates
events.summary: Reza Shah abdicated in favour of his son Mohammad Reza.

events.title: Tripartite Treaty of Alliance
events.summary: Iran, Britain and the USSR signed a treaty: Allied powers to respect Iran's independence and withdraw within six months of the end of hostilities.

events.title: Tehran Conference
events.summary: Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin reaffirmed commitment to Iran's independence and territorial integrity.

events.title: Reza Shah dies in Johannesburg
events.summary: LoC: died in July 1944 in Johannesburg. Day (26 July) per Wikipedia.

events.title: Soviet withdrawal; Azarbaijan and Mahabad republics collapse
events.summary: Soviet troops withdrew in 1946 under US, British and UN pressure; the autonomous Azarbaijan government and the Kurdish Republic of Mahabad collapsed after the army entered Azarbaijan in December 1946.

events.title: Majlis votes to nationalise the oil industry
events.summary: Followed in April by Mohammad Mossadeq's appointment as prime minister; Britain imposed an embargo.

events.title: ICJ judgment: no jurisdiction
events.summary: The International Court of Justice decided it had no jurisdiction in the Anglo-Iranian Oil Co. case brought by the UK.
events.note: LoC loc17 says the court 'found in Iran's favor'. That is not what the ICJ's own overview says. Do not repeat the LoC wording.

events.title: Overthrow of Mossadeq
events.summary: Pro-shah army units and street crowds defeated Mossadeq's forces on 19 August 1953, after an initial attempt had appeared to fail and the shah had left the country; the shah returned. A joint US-UK operation (CIA 'TPAJAX'/'Ajax') is documented; the exact balance of foreign and Iranian roles is disputed by historians.
events.note: Sequence (13 Aug dismissal of Mossadeq; shah leaves; 19 Aug) per loc17; roles contested per NSA.

events.title: Marriage to Farah Diba
events.summary: LoC: the shah remarried in 1959; the crown prince Reza was born in 1960.

events.title: Land distribution law approved
events.summary: Approved by the cabinet under Prime Minister Ali Amini.

events.title: White Revolution referendum
events.summary: Six measures put to a national referendum; the government announced a 99 per cent majority.
events.note: Official figure; the referendum was not an independent poll.

events.title: Women's suffrage announced
events.summary: The shah announced the extension of the vote to women.

events.title: Khomeini arrested; three days of riots
events.summary: After a speech attacking the shah, Ayatollah Khomeini was arrested in Qom; three days of violent riots followed and were severely suppressed.

events.title: Khomeini exiled
events.summary: Arrested after a sermon against the Status of Forces bill and sent to Turkey; from October 1965 he lived in An Najaf, Iraq.

events.title: Prime Minister Mansur assassinated
events.summary: Hasan Ali Mansur was assassinated; Amir Abbas Hoveyda became prime minister and served for twelve years.

events.title: Coronation of Mohammad Reza Shah
events.summary: LoC: 'In October 1967' the shah celebrated his long-postponed coronation and placed the crown on his own head; the Majlis conferred the title Arya-Mehr.
events.note: Day (26 Oct) from Wikipedia; month and year from LoC.

events.title: Shiraz Arts Festival
events.summary: Annual international arts festival held in Shiraz and Persepolis, initiated by Farah Pahlavi.
events.note: Single tertiary source. Upgrade to an Iranica or festival-archive citation before publication.

events.title: Shahyad (Azadi) Tower completed
events.summary: Designed by Hossein Amanat; commissioned to mark the celebrations; renamed Azadi Tower after 1979.
events.note: Tertiary only; verify with Iranica or the architect's own record.

events.title: Siahkal attack
events.summary: The Fadayan launched the first major guerrilla action against the state with an attack on a gendarmerie post at Siahkal.

events.title: 2,500-year celebrations at Persepolis
events.summary: Festivities marking 2,500 years of the Iranian empire began on 12 October 1971. LoC records adverse domestic comment and Khomeini's declaration condemning them.

events.title: Nixon's visit; arms purchase policy
events.summary: During his 1972 visit Nixon allowed the shah to buy any conventional US weapon in the quantities he judged necessary.

events.title: One-party state; calendar change; Algiers Agreement
events.summary: The Rastakhiz party created a one-party state; the Majlis changed the calendar to begin with Cyrus's reign; Iran and Iraq signed the Algiers Agreement.

events.title: Tehran Museum of Contemporary Art opens
events.summary: Inaugurated by Farah Pahlavi; designed by Kamran Diba with Nader Ardalan.
events.note: Tertiary only; upgrade to museum or Iranica source.

events.title: Hoveyda replaced by Amuzegar; limited liberalisation
events.summary: After Carter took office the shah released some political prisoners and replaced Hoveyda after twelve years.

events.title: Ettelaat article; Qom protests
events.summary: A government-inspired newspaper article about Khomeini provoked protests in Qom in which several demonstrators were killed; memorial protests spread in February.

events.title: Rex Cinema fire, Abadan
events.summary: More than 400 people died. LoC notes that evidence after the revolution suggested deliberate arson by religiously inclined students, while the opposition cultivated the belief that SAVAK was responsible.
events.note: Responsibility remains disputed in public memory; attribute precisely.

events.title: Jaleh Square shooting ('Black Friday')
events.summary: Troops fired on demonstrators after martial law was declared in Tehran and eleven other cities. LoC: 'certainly many more' died than the official figure of eighty-seven.
events.note: Casualty figures contested; state official figure and LoC caveat only.

events.title: Military government under General Azhari
events.summary: The shah replaced Sharif-Emami with General Gholam-Reza Azhari after violent demonstrations in Tehran.

events.title: Persepolis inscribed on the World Heritage List
events.summary: UNESCO inscribed Persepolis in 1979.

events.title: The shah leaves Iran
events.summary: Announced as a 'short holiday'; celebrations broke out as his aircraft took off.

events.title: Khomeini returns to Tehran
events.summary: Received by millions; named Mehdi Bazargan prime minister of a provisional government on 5 February.

events.title: Armed forces declare neutrality; monarchy collapses
events.summary: On 11 February twenty-two senior commanders declared neutrality; by the late afternoon of 12 February Bakhtiar was in hiding and the Pahlavi monarchy had collapsed (LoC).

events.title: Mohammad Reza Pahlavi dies in Cairo
events.summary: Died in exile in Egypt at age 60; state funeral held in Cairo on 30 July.
events.note: Funeral date and burial at Al-Rifa'i Mosque: Wikipedia only (not in tier A/B sources yet).

events.title: Golestan Palace inscribed by UNESCO
events.summary: The Qajar-era palace complex in Tehran became a World Heritage Site.
